transcript:
[00:00] Rachel Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Rachel (Redwood), Samir (Redwood), Evelyn, Darren, Maya from Mistral. We're planning 45 minutes, we'll focus on cost/unit economics and governance.
[00:18] Evelyn Park: Yep, thanks. We're short on time, so maybe start with our top constraints — we have a hard monthly token spend target and also strict encryption/residency rules.
[00:30] Samir Patel: Got it. Can you remind us what your current architecture looks like for inference? GPU cluster, cloud endpoints?
[00:40] Darren O'Neill: Right now it's a mix — internal CPU-based microservices for light tasks, and we spin up GPU VMs in GCP for heavy workloads. We pay per-instance and it's messy. We don't want to manage the stack long term.
[00:55] Maya Flores: From FinOps: our cap is roughly $40k/month for model inference for Q1 pilot, and that's firm. We need to see unit economics that fit — per-token or per-call.
[01:10] Rachel Kim: OK, that's helpful. On Redwood's side we typically break this into per-token hosted pricing, or reserved capacity for Dedicated which gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost. There's also Private for VPC/on-prem if compliance requires.
[01:26] Evelyn Park: Two big questions: 1) how much can batching and prefix/KV caching reduce per-token costs, and 2) what security controls you provide for audit/auditor requests.
[01:38] Samir Patel: On batching and caching — typical wins depend on request shape. If you have many repeated prefixes or similar prompts, prefix caching (we sometimes call it KV cache) can reduce compute by reusing KV state for tokens. Batching helps when requests arrive concurrently — it amortizes kernel cost across tokens.
[01:56] Darren O'Neill: When you say KV cache — is that sticky to a customer session? We saw it called "K-V cash" in a doc ha — transcription mismatch — but we mean state reuse.
[02:08] Samir Patel: Yes — it's customer-specific and configurable. For privacy we can scope the cache to a customer key and TTL. It reduces tokens executed on GPU, not per-token billed but reduces compute charge which then lowers effective unit cost.
[02:21] Maya Flores: So is billing still per token even if cache hits? How do we model that in our budget?
[02:30] Rachel Kim: For hosted API we bill per-token served (input+output). Caching may reduce the number of tokens executed which lowers cost on our backend; from a pricing standpoint we have two levers: the published per-token rate and then we can offer model-specific batch discounts or pilot credits. For Dedicated you commit to capacity and get a lower effective per-token cost because the GPU amortization is fixed.
[02:49] Evelyn Park: Can you give an example — maybe a 2,048-seq model with 75% caching hit rate?
[03:00] Samir Patel: Example numbers: naive per-token hosted might be $0.0008/token for that model at our list price. With a 75% prefix/cache hit rate the effective compute at runtime drops, so the equivalent cost might be more like $0.00035/token because a lot of decoding is skipped. But again, hosted list price remains; we typically model that as an expected effective unit cost for your workload and then propose pilot discounts.
[03:22] Darren O'Neill: Hmm, those numbers are big swings. We need a spreadsheet to plug our average prompt lengths and hit rates.
[03:30] Rachel Kim: We'll send a worksheet. Samir can also run your sample prompts through a 24-hour hosted benchmark so you get empirical numbers.
[03:38] Maya Flores: Good. Security: we need SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML, KMS integration for key control, and audit logs retained 12 months. Can Redwood provide those?
[03:54] Samir Patel: Yes — hosted offers SOC2 docs, SAML SSO, and for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS and longer audit retention. Hosted uses encrypted-at-rest with our KMS, but for Dedicated we can help integrate your KMS/HSM in the VPC.
[04:11] Evelyn Park: Is Private only for on-prem? Or can Private be VPC-hosted with customer-managed keys?
[04:18] Rachel Kim: Private is our flexible option — can be VPC with customer KMS, or an on-prem package. It adds ops overhead but gives you the KMS/HSM integration and full control over network egress.
[04:30] Darren O'Neill: From ops: we're nervous about performance variability on hosted during peak. Does Redwood provide burst capacity or guaranteed latency?
[04:40] Samir Patel: For Hosted we provide best-effort SLAs; for predictable SLOs we recommend Dedicated with reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies that you control. Dedicated has an SLA tier for uptime and latency and predictable throughput.
[04:53] Maya Flores: If Dedicated reduces unit cost, how big a commitment are we talking? We only have $40k for pilot month 1.
[05:02] Rachel Kim: Dedicated minimums vary by region and model family, but we can structure a short-term reserved commitment to prove economics. Another pattern is run a hosted pilot first, measure effective unit economics after caching and batching, then move to Dedicated with a 3–6 month commit if it makes sense.
[05:18] Evelyn Park: Timeline — we want a pilot running in November. Is that realistic?
[05:23] Samir Patel: Yes. If you share sample prompts and forecast, we can stand up a hosted benchmark in a few days and have a results deck within a week.
[05:33] Rachel Kim: Quick qualification: what percent of requests are synchronous low-latency (sub-300ms) vs async batch? That changes strategy.
[05:42] Darren O'Neill: Most are low-latency chat-type calls (~60%), then a 30% async scoring batch overnight, and 10% other.
[05:52] Samir Patel: That mix is very typical. For low-latency hosted with caching and continuous batching you still get benefits; for large overnight batches Dedicated can be more cost-efficient. So you'll likely run a hybrid model.
[06:05] Maya Flores: How do you handle multi-tenant and data isolation? We need tenant-level audit trails.
[06:14] Samir Patel: We emit tenant-level logs, and Dedicated/Private can provide network isolation plus customer-managed keys. Hosted has RBAC and token-level metrics but not customer KMS isolation.
[06:26] Evelyn Park: Competitors — we spoke to Anthropic and tried a PoC with them. Costs were... opaque. How does Redwood compare in transparency?
[06:34] Rachel Kim: We aim for transparent unit economics and a calculator. We'll include a cost model that shows how batching, caching, quantization, and routing policies change your effective unit price.
[06:45] Darren O'Neill: Quantization — can you run 8-bit models to reduce cost with little quality loss?
[06:51] Samir Patel: Yes, we support quantized variants and will recommend per-model quantization profiles. That reduces memory and can often improve throughput, which feeds into lower unit cost. It's part of Redwood Optimize.
[07:03] Maya Flores: Any hidden surcharges for egress or KV cache?
[07:07] Rachel Kim: No hidden egress on hosted for standard regions — pricing is per-token and listed. For Dedicated you pay the reserved capacity and any infra add-ons. We'll be explicit in the pricing sheet.
[07:18] Evelyn Park: Ok, let's talk pilot scope. We want to validate: 1) sustained 800 rps during peak batch window, 2) effective per-token < $0.0005 after caching, 3) no blockers on security list.
[07:33] Samir Patel: Those are measurable KPIs. For 800 rps we need to understand average sequence length and concurrency — we'll size the test.
[07:41] Darren O'Neill: Avg prompt length 120 tokens in, 320 tokens out for chat; batch jobs are up to 2,000 tokens per item.
[07:51] Samir Patel: Noted. We'll run both chat-shaped traffic and overnight batch. For the batch, batching will help a lot; the overnight window is where Dedicated can dramatically lower cost per token.
[08:02] Maya Flores: If we see the economics work, what would a minimal Dedicated deal look like? 3-month commit? 6-month?
[08:09] Rachel Kim: Typical is 3–12 months. For pilots we propose a 3-month trial with a ramp schedule and an option to convert credits into reserved capacity if you commit. We'll outline options.
[08:21] Evelyn Park: Auditability: Can we get log exports into our Splunk/Datadog?
[08:27] Samir Patel: Yes — we can provide log hooks and trace exports. For Dedicated/Private, you can host the forwarder in your VPC. Hosted has webhooks and S3 export as well.
[08:37] Darren O'Neill: Latency numbers under load — do you have p95 for the model families?
[08:43] Samir Patel: We have benchmark decks per model. Roughly for the model family you're looking at, p95 on a dedicated GPU node is sub-200ms for 512 tokens; for 2k tokens p95 grows and batching helps. We'll include relevant charts.
[08:59] Rachel Kim: Quick interruption — Maya, you said the $40k is for month 1 only? Or monthly baseline?
[09:06] Maya Flores: Month 1 pilot is $40k; long term we expect that to change but procurement needs the pilot to hit that number.
[09:12] Rachel Kim: Understood. We'll propose a hosted pilot plan that fits within $40k to validate and then show Dedicated savings if you want to scale.
[09:20] Evelyn Park: Data residency — some customers require EU-only. We have EU users; can we pin region?
[09:27] Samir Patel: Yes. Hosted can pin region for model runs; Dedicated obviously lives in chosen region; Private gives you full control.
[09:33] Darren O'Neill: Any friction integrating with our SSO and SCIM?
[09:38] Rachel Kim: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. We'll include an admin guide.
[09:44] Maya Flores: Pricing sensitivity — if your hosted per-token is above our threshold we won't consider it. What wiggle room do you have?
[09:54] Rachel Kim: We can offer pilot credits and a pilot-specific per-token discount. If the pilot proves high cache or batching wins, a Dedicated conversion will typically reduce unit costs further.
[10:05] Evelyn Park: Let's talk modeling briefly — what variables do you need to calculate effective unit cost?
[10:10] Samir Patel: We need average prompt length (in tokens), output length, request arrival distribution (concurrency), cache hit rate, and batch window characteristics. Also which model family and sequence length cap.
[10:23] Darren O'Neill: We'll share a sample of 1,000 prompts and forecast.
[10:28] Maya Flores: We'll anonymize any PII.
[10:31] Rachel Kim: Great. We'll run that through an on-hosted benchmark and share a spreadsheet with modeled outcomes.
[10:39] Evelyn Park: Any implementation gotchas for our engineers when switching from instance-based to Redwood?
[10:44] Samir Patel: Main differences: use the Redwood API for calls, consider session affinity if you rely on KV cache, and optionally integrate our SDK for efficient client-side batching. We'll provide sample code and a confluence doc.
[10:58] Darren O'Neill: Can you support rate limiting or token caps per tenant? We need guardrails for runaway prompts.
[11:06] Samir Patel: Yes — per-API-key rate limits and per-tenant quotas are supported. You can set hard caps and alerts.
[11:14] Rachel Kim: Okay, we're about halfway through, do we want to move to specific pilot next steps?
[11:20] Maya Flores: Yes. We want to see a hosted-run benchmark, a cost model, and your SOC2 + KMS notes.
[11:28] Rachel Kim: Action items then: 1) I'll send the pricing sheet and workbook, 2) Samir will run a 24-hr benchmark on hosted using your sample prompts, 3) we'll share SOC2 and security appendix.
[11:40] Evelyn Park: Sounds good. A quick note — if we need Private for audit reasons, how long does on-prem deployment take?
[11:47] Samir Patel: On-prem delivery is typically 6–10 weeks depending on integration depth. VPC/private with customer-managed KMS is faster, typically 2–4 weeks.
[11:58] Darren O'Neill: Maya, any procurement constraints beyond the $40k pilot?
[12:02] Maya Flores: PO terms standard, we need vendor security questionnaire answered before PO.
[12:07] Samir Patel: We can start security questionnaire now and return answers within 3 business days.
[12:14] Rachel Kim: OK, last 10 minutes — let's recap and pick a date for the deep-tech session. Would the week of 2026-10-27 work?
[12:22] Evelyn Park: Yes, afternoons EST work best.
[12:26] Rachel Kim: Great. We'll tentatively schedule a technical deep dive for Oct 28.
[12:31] Darren O'Neill: Any final quick questions?
[12:34] Maya Flores: No, just please make the cost workbook easy to edit.
[12:38] Samir Patel: Will do.
[12:41] Rachel Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the sheet, security pack, and benchmark plan within 48 hours.
[12:50] Evelyn Park: Thanks all.
[12:53] Darren O'Neill: Thanks.
[12:55] Maya Flores: Bye.
